summary: ECOWAS citizens enter Ghana without a visa, African Union citizens apply online for an AU ETA, and ten Caribbean passports and Singapore qualify for their own ETA; most other visitors need an eVisa (USD 260, up to 60 days) from the Ghana Immigration Service portal or a visa from a Ghanaian embassy.

safety.text: Ghana is one of West Africa's most stable countries. Petty theft and street scams occur in Accra. The UK Foreign Office advises against all but essential travel to the Bawku Municipal area in the Upper East region, and the far-northern border areas adjoining Burkina Faso call for extra caution because of regional insecurity.

tips.text: African Union citizens outside ECOWAS are no longer visa-free: the Ghana Immigration Service portal requires an AU ETA, applied for online before travel, which replaces the visa on arrival.

Use the eligibility checker on evisa.immigration.gov.gh before you book: it tells you whether your passport needs an eVisa, an ETA or nothing at all. Do not count on a visa at the airport: the only visa on arrival is the Emergency Entry Visa, which your host must get approved before you fly.

Carry your yellow fever certificate. The Ghana Immigration Service says it is required for entry and may be checked at the port of entry, and that travellers without one may be referred to airport health officials, including for vaccination.
Canada's travel advice says malaria is a risk to travellers to Ghana and recommends antimalarial medication for most of them. Talk to a travel health clinic before you go, and use insect repellent.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Ghana?
faq.answer: It depends on your passport. ECOWAS citizens need neither a visa nor an ETA. Citizens of other African Union countries need an AU ETA, and a few Caribbean countries and Singapore have their own ETA. Most other nationalities, including the US, UK and EU, need a visa: an eVisa from the Ghana Immigration Service portal (USD 260, up to 60 days) or a visa from a Ghanaian embassy or high commission.

faq.question: Do US citizens need a visa for Ghana?
faq.answer: Yes. US passport holders need a visa before travel. They can apply online for a Ghana eVisa on the Ghana Immigration Service portal: USD 260 with standard processing within 96 hours, single entry, a stay of up to 60 days (the immigration officer sets it on arrival), valid 90 days from issue. A visa from a Ghanaian embassy or consulate remains an alternative.

faq.question: Is Ghana visa-free for African passport holders?
faq.answer: Only for ECOWAS citizens, who need neither a visa nor an ETA and may stay up to 90 days. Citizens of the other African Union countries must apply online for an AU ETA before travel; it is single-entry and valid for 90 days, and the portal says it replaces the visa on arrival.

faq.question: Can I get a visa on arrival in Ghana?
faq.answer: Only with approval arranged before you travel. The Ghana Immigration Service's visa on arrival is the Emergency Entry Visa: your host in Ghana applies to GIS headquarters, the fee is USD 200, and you carry the approval letter to check-in and to Kotoka airport. There is no walk-up visa on arrival, and the AU ETA replaces it for African Union citizens. Most visitors should get an eVisa or an embassy visa instead.

faq.question: Do I need a yellow fever vaccination for Ghana?
faq.answer: Yes. All travelers aged 9 months and over must show a valid yellow fever vaccination certificate on arrival. This applies to every nationality, including visa-free visitors.
